name: Monocoupe 90 / 110
summary: Small two-seat high-wing 1930s sport and racing monoplane with a distinctive reverse-curve rear fuselage; remembered for air racing and aerobatics.

engines: Small radial engine (Lambert or Warner) in the nose, often with cylinders partly exposed
fuselage: Two seats side by side in a small enclosed cabin with side doors
Fixed tailwheel gear, often with wheel pants

tellTales: Tiny two-seat high-wing monoplane with a small radial engine
Rear fuselage dips in a reverse curve behind the cabin
Side-by-side seating in a compact cabin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Luscombe is all-metal with a flat-four engine and a smoother fuselage line; the Monocoupe has a small radial and a distinctive reverse-curve rear fuselage.
The Citabria has tandem seating, a flat-four engine and a straight fuselage; the Monocoupe seats two side by side with a radial.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
